note: Facts only. 292 moons: JPL Horizons' list. Three groups of irregular moons (Inuit, Gallic, Norse) and the regular moons. Radius basis 'measured' is a published measurement, 'estimate' is brightness-based (an assumed albedo of 0.04). One moon, S/2009 S 2 (announced June 2026), has no published size; its radius 0.15 km is a stand-in equal to the 0.3 km moonlet S/2009 S 1 that the same source lists beside it, marked estimate. Daphnis's curve fit covers only 2010 to 2018 (see its index entry). Moons with a bodyPackage use the O-018 packages unchanged.

families.label: The seven big moons
families.description: Mimas, Enceladus, Tethys, Dione, Rhea, Titan and Iapetus: massive enough to be round. Each has a Planetary Explorer map.

families.label: Small regular moons
families.description: The small moons on regular orbits: the ring shepherds and ring moonlets close to Saturn (Pan to Pallene), the pair Janus and Epimetheus that swap orbits, the Trojan moons of Tethys and Dione, and Hyperion.

families.label: Inuit group
families.description: Irregular moons on prograde orbits, 190 to 300 Saturn radii out, inclined 43 to 51 degrees, taken to be pieces of one or a few parent bodies; the Kiviuq and Siarnaq subgroups.

families.label: Gallic group
families.description: Irregular moons on prograde orbits inclined 34 to 41 degrees, taken to be pieces of one parent body; the largest is Albiorix.

families.label: Norse group
families.description: All retrograde irregular moons, the largest group by far; Phoebe is the biggest. Ashton et al. 2025 split it by inclination into the Phoebe, Mundilfari, Kari and low-inclination subgroups.
